# D2 — primitive direct-carrier birth from sealed-diamond amalgamation

**Status:** preregistered before the D2 production receipt, 2026-07-11. No
result may be promoted outside an executed gate.

## 1. Question

Can the existing sealed-diamond ontology derive a primitive direct carrier
from a committed marked history, without presupposing:

- a global construction order;
- emergent distance;
- an already shared ancestor;
- a manually supplied overlap/interface map;
- hidden labels or a future outcome;
- a free pair-versus-hyperedge selector?

D1 showed that no-silent closure operates only after a candidate cut has been
supplied. D2 moves one step upstream and asks whether diamond amalgamation can
supply that cut.

There is a foundational fork. If a full non-Markovian probability measure on
variable marked histories is primitive, it already supplies both the candidate
event domain and `P(next|full committed history)`. D2 then tests only a
representation/consistency property of that supplied law. The derivation
question exists only in the stronger SHARD program that asks sealed record
structure to determine the history measure rather than positing it.

## 2. Corpus basis

The relevant inherited results are:

1. v6 defines a sealed diamond by finite records, lower/upper screens,
   collars, transports, and a whole-history law.
2. v6 eventless collar gluing cancels artificial internal seams once a global
   interface cochain is supplied.
3. v6 overlap/sheaf consistency says local diamonds must be restrictions of
   one coherent whole-history law, but leaves continuous families of local and
   hidden global holonomy coefficients.
4. v7 classifies overlap transport as one primitive diamond interface, but its
   seed list and overlap maps remain conditional axioms.
5. v9 construction diamonds show that update order can be gauge after the
   physical incidences and local kernels are fixed.
6. D1 shows that a supplied direct-carrier/output-port axiom can enforce
   structural locality, but no-silent residue does not derive the carrier and
   its eligible-support family is not projective.

The live possibility is therefore conditional:

> a typed overlap diagram may determine a canonical amalgam even though the
> history does not determine which overlap diagram should be used.

## 3. Frozen finite ontology

A D2 boundary object is a finite marked support system

$$
D=(V,E,m),
$$

where:

- `V` is a finite set of record/port identifiers;
- `E` is a finite family of direct supports with cardinality at least two;
- `m(v)=(t,p)` is a finite port/interface type and stable
  provenance/ancestry mark.

The executable category uses mark-preserving **weak support homomorphisms**:
vertices may be identified, and the image of every support must be a target
support whenever at least two distinct image vertices remain. General
morphisms need not be injective; supplied interface legs must be injective.
This distinction is required for coproduct/pushout universal properties.

A restriction retains a vertex set `K`. D2 distinguishes two support
projections:

1. **intersection/shadow projection**

   $$
   r_K(E)=\{e\cap K:e\in E,\ |e\cap K|\ge2\};
   $$

2. **contained-event projection**

   $$
   q_K(E)=\{e\in E:e\subseteq K\}.
   $$

They encode different physical claims. The first says a higher support leaves
lower-support shadows. The second says an irreducible event disappears when
any participant is removed. Neither may be silently substituted for the
other.

## 4. Typed marked-support amalgam

A gluing diagram is a span

$$
D_A\xleftarrow{f}I\xrightarrow{g}D_B,
$$

where `I` is a supplied interface and `f,g` are supplied injective
mark-preserving maps. Its finite pushout identifies `f(i)` with `g(i)` and
takes the union of transported supports and marks.

The universal construction is allowed to determine the amalgam **given the
span**. It is not allowed to claim that the universal property selected `I`,
`f`, or `g`.

## 5. Expected positive theorem

For a fixed compatible typed diagram:

1. the finite pushout exists;
2. it is unique up to marked isomorphism;
3. compatible iterated pushouts are independent of serial construction order;
4. artificial internal interfaces do not create an additional source/support;
5. the support family of the pushout is generated by transported input
   supports, with no unlicensed cross-support.

This is a conditional composition and construction-gauge theorem.

## 6. Mandatory no-go attacks

### A1 — empty-interface no-bootstrap

The pushout over the empty interface is the disjoint coproduct. It must not
create a cross-component pair or hyperedge.

### A2 — nonempty overlap does not create exclusive cross-support

For `A={a,i}` and `B={i,b}`, ordinary union gluing may inherit paths through
`i`, but it must not silently add `{a,b}` or `{a,i,b}`.

### A3 — interface-map ambiguity

Construct two isomorphic bare interfaces with two different embeddings whose
pushouts are nonisomorphic. If successful, covariance and the pushout
universal property do not select the gluing legs.

### A4 — first-pair projectivity theorem

Enumerate every extensive deterministic pair-edge closure on labeled histories
through three vertices. Require:

- permutation covariance;
- idempotence;
- commutation with every induced vertex restriction;
- refusal to add an edge to an edgeless two-record support skeleton.

Test whether any operator can add a first pair edge.

### A5 — higher-support ambiguity

Allow one three-record support in addition to its three pair faces. Under
intersection/shadow restriction, enumerate all covariant extensive idempotent
fill rules. Test whether both “leave the boundary unfilled” and “fill the
complete triangle” survive.

### A6 — restriction-semantics dependence

Repeat the empty-to-triple proposal under contained-event restriction. If the
proposal becomes projective only because every pair restriction discards the
triple, record the dependence on the chosen restriction ontology.

### A7 — automorphism obstruction

On three structurally identical output ports, test whether a deterministic
covariant rule can select exactly one pair. Also test the exact uniform
stochastic kernel. A stochastic kernel may be covariant even when no
deterministic selector exists; it must then face the same strong restriction
and two-record-refusal gate. Construction order may not act as a hidden
symmetry breaker.

### A8 — common-root control

An inherited common-root carrier may project to descendant supports. This is a
restriction of supplied ancestry, not creation of a new primitive carrier.

## 7. Exact gates

### G0 — self-containment

Every D2 source file is under `v10/code/`, imports only the Python standard
library as verified by parsing its import tree, and is run with
`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`.

### G1 — canonical fixed-span pushout

Define the ambient marked-support category and verify canonical maps plus the
unique mediator for every valid cocone into a finite audit target. Relabeling
the diagram transports the pushout to an isomorphic marked support system.

### G2 — construction-order gauge

Two true iterated typed-pushout presentations of a three-diamond diagram
produce marked-isomorphic amalgams.

### G3 — support conservation

The pushout contains exactly the transported input supports; no cross-support
is invented by gluing.

### G4 — map-selection attack

If different legal interface embeddings yield nonisomorphic pushouts, grade
the interface selector `OPEN`.

### G5 — first-carrier no-go

If exhaustive pair-closure enumeration leaves only the identity operator,
prove the finite support-skeleton theorem and refuse primitive pair birth only
under the frozen axioms.

### G6 — hyperedge selector

If two or more higher-support fill operators survive, grade arity/filling
`FAMILY`, not unique.

### G7 — restriction ontology

Every projectivity statement names intersection/shadow or contained-event
restriction explicitly.

### G8 — symmetry

No presentation order or integer label may select one member of a nontrivial
automorphism orbit. A uniform stochastic orbit kernel is reported as an
additional law and tested for strong restriction naturality; it is not omitted
merely because deterministic selection fails.

### G9 — D1 handoff

No-silent closure is applied only after a candidate span/carrier is supplied.
D2 does not use D1 residue to manufacture a span.

## 8. Verdict map

### AMALGAMATION-POSITIVE

Fixed typed spans have canonical, construction-order-gauge pushouts.

### CARRIER-BIRTH-POSITIVE

Allowed only if the committed history uniquely determines the interface,
embeddings, arity, and new support while passing both restriction semantics or
deriving why only one is physical.

### CONDITIONAL-COMPOSITION / BIRTH-REFUSAL

If a span determines an amalgam but the span itself is unselected, diamond
amalgamation is composition rather than carrier birth.

### PROJECTIVITY-NO-BOOTSTRAP

If restriction plus edgeless-pair refusal forbids a first pair carrier, a new
bridge needs an initial/root law or new boundary sector.

### FAMILY

If several covariant projective higher-support rules survive, no unique
carrier law has been derived.

## 9. Claim ceiling

D2 may establish an exact finite categorical/combinatorial theorem. It may
not claim:

- relativistic microcausality;
- a continuum or profinite extension;
- a firing probability or transfer coefficient;
- quantum entanglement dynamics;
- geometry or a round cone;
- that a categorical universal property creates its own input diagram.

## 10. Review protocol

After the receipt and Paper 3 draft exist, three independent hostile reviews
will audit:

1. exact combinatorics/category and restriction theorems;
2. independent reconstruction and adversary search;
3. ontology, locality, symmetry, and claim scope.

Every concrete opening is investigated before the next review round.

### O1 — hostile round 1 openings

All three referees reproduced the 20/20 incidence receipt but required major
revision before round 2:

1. define an ambient morphism category; injection-only maps do not admit the
   claimed empty coproduct, so general weak homomorphisms and injective
   interface legs must be separated;
2. implement marks, types, provenance, mark-preserving leg validation, and a
   genuine typed pushout rather than calling shared-label union “typed”;
3. execute a universal-factorization audit and true iterated typed pushouts;
4. make ancestry provenance load-bearing in interface admissibility;
5. state explicitly that the marked-support system is a forgetful support
   skeleton of a sealed diamond, not its full stochastic/holonomy law;
6. add the exact covariant stochastic `1/3` pair kernel and test its strong
   projectivity;
7. enumerate the contained-event fill family rather than displaying one
   example;
8. validate injective bare-graph legs, assert the exact surviving fill
   predicates, and make the self-containment gate inspect imports.
